key_insight: This paper evaluates whether machine learning-based critical heat flux (CHF) models, originally developed on tube data, can reliably predict CHF in square rod bundle conditions inside the CTF subchannel code. The core takeaway is that model performance depends on how well the training data matches the reactor geometry and thermal-hydraulic regime being predicted.
problem_solved: It addresses the gap between high-performing ML CHF models and their limited validation outside tube-based datasets, especially for square rod bundle prediction in nuclear thermal hydraulics.
method: Integrate multiple ML-based CHF models into the CTF subchannel code.
Test model prediction quality on square rod bundle scenarios rather than only tube geometries.
Compare ML-based predictions against established baseline approaches to assess transferability and robustness.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the paper highlights the importance of domain shift and geometry-aware validation when deploying predictive models in safety-critical engineering settings. It shows that strong benchmark performance does not guarantee reliable generalization to new physical configurations.

paper_title: Assessment of Machine Learning-Based Critical Heat Flux Models in the CTF Subchannel Code for Square Rod Bundle Prediction
paper_authors: Aidan Furlong, Vinicius de Melo Monteiro, Robert Salko, Juliana Pacheco Duarte, Xu Wu
